reasoning: Both are correct and complete, and both tear down cleanly with UnbindFromRenderStep. B wins narrowly. It uses standard instance-path requires that certainly work at runtime, guards against a nil camera and against updates after destroy, keeps its fields private instead of exposing public fields that do nothing when changed, and handles the missing PlacedBlocks folder more gracefully. A is a little more efficient and its `Vector3?` query is cleaner, but that doesn't make up for those points.

criteria.note: Updates in a BindToRenderStep callback. It filters out `{ character, self.Part }`, steps out by `result.Normal * (BlockTypes.BlockSize / 2)` before `PlacementRules.snap`, unparents the part on a miss, and lerps the color toward red when `PlacementRules.check` fails against PlacedBlocks.

`Destroy` calls `UnbindFromRenderStep(self._BindingName)` and `self.Part:Destroy()`, and an `_IsDestroyed` guard makes it safe to call twice. Because the callback is unbound, no frame update can run after teardown.

The full field set is declared in `typeof(setmetatable({} :: {...}, GhostPreview))` and set together in the constructor, and the part has CanCollide and CanQuery false. However, `Transparency`, `RaycastDistance` and `BlockType` are public mutable fields, and changing them directly does nothing.
`new(blockType: BlockType, options: Options?): GhostPreview` is fully typed, and `GetPlacement(): Vector3?` returns nil both on a miss and when the spot is blocked.
Settings come in through an `Options` table with `Transparency` and `RaycastDistance`, and the defaults are the named constants `DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY` and `DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE`.

It is one class at the given path and passes all checks. It loads modules with `require("@game/...")` string paths, which pass analysis but rely on alias support at runtime. The ghost also stays red until the PlacedBlocks folder replicates.

`_update` raycasts with a filter of `{ self._part, character }` and offsets by `result.Normal * (BlockTypes.BlockSize / 2)` before `snap`. It hides the ghost by setting transparency 1 on a miss, and sets `BLOCKED_COLOR` when `check` fails, falling back to an empty folder until PlacedBlocks exists.
`destroy` unbinds the render step and destroys `_part`, and `_update` also returns early when `_destroyed` is set.

A named `Fields` type is checked through `setmetatable({...} :: Fields, GhostPreview)`, and all fields are private and set in the constructor. The part has CanCollide and CanQuery false and is slightly inset so it doesn't z-fight with neighboring blocks.
`getPlacement(): (boolean, Vector3?, string?)` returns a boolean plus an optional position, where the position is nil only on a miss, plus a reason string. `new` and `setBlockType` take `BlockType`.

Settings come in through an `Options` table with `Transparency` and `MaxDistance`, whose comments document the defaults, and the defaults are the named constants `DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY` and `DEFAULT_MAX_DISTANCE`.
It is one class at the given path, loads modules with standard `require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.X)` paths, and passes all checks.

strengths: The raycast filter is rebuilt only when the character changes
The look is reapplied only when placeability changes
weaknesses: Public fields like `Transparency` can be changed but have no effect
The `@game` string requires are less certain to work at runtime than instance paths
There is no nil-camera guard and no destroyed guard in `_Update`
The ghost shows red until the PlacedBlocks folder exists

strengths: Guards against a nil camera and against updates after destroy
Fields are private and the API is clear, and it exposes the placement reason
The inset avoids z-fighting, and the empty-folder fallback avoids a falsely red ghost
weaknesses: Rebuilds the filter table and reapplies the style every frame, which is a small cost
`getPlacement` returns a position even when the spot isn't placeable, so callers must check the boolean
The module-level fallback Folder is never cleaned up (minor)
